scope: Additional land airports and selected floatplane terminals and heliports. The main branding register covers the priority land airports.
method: Checked airport, operator and local government pages, downloaded candidate artwork where accessible and inspected the visible marks and file contents.

statusDefinitions.verified-vector: Native vector geometry verified in the terminal or airport publisher's asset.
statusDefinitions.verified-raster: Airport-specific signature verified in the publisher's raster asset.
statusDefinitions.documented-raster-lead: Documented signature whose standalone artwork remains to be recovered.
statusDefinitions.documented-raster-composite: Verified branding integrated into a banner or background image.
statusDefinitions.shared-identity: The facility is presented as part of another airport or airpark.
statusDefinitions.carrier-brand-only: The checked material shows a carrier's identity.
statusDefinitions.operator-brand-only: The checked material shows the operator or owner's identity.
statusDefinitions.no-separate-mark-found: No separate airport identity verified in the checked sources.

airports.name: 100 Mile House Municipal Airport
airports.notes: District airport page and published master plan use District branding. Separate from South Cariboo Regional Airport near 108 Mile Ranch.

airports.name: Alert Bay Airport (H.J. Pickup Airport)
airports.notes: The Village lists the airstrip and maintains a 2026–2041 Airport Master Plan. Inspect master plan cover and airport entry signage for a facility signature.

airports.name: Atlin Airport (Peterson Field)
airports.notes: 300 × 97 transparent official site signature. The association and the publisher credited at the bottom of the airport website are leads for an original vector.

artwork.label: Atlin Airport website lockup
artwork.locator: Full-size source in the header logo srcset

airports.name: Avey Field State Airport
airports.notes: Cross-border record. WSDOT identifies the facility near Laurier, Washington. The state guide and airport page carry state-agency branding.

airports.name: Burns Lake Airport
airports.notes: 1800 × 450 official illustrated banner with uppercase airport name, airplane and helicopter. Useful as a branding specimen. Search the Airport Society's publications and terminal signage for a standalone mark.

artwork.label: Illustrated Burns Lake Airport web banner
artwork.locator: Original image path referenced by the homepage Next.js banner

airports.name: Chetwynd Municipal Airport
airports.notes: The official municipal page names the airport and shows webcam images. District airport documents and terminal signage are further leads.

airports.name: Courtenay Airpark
airports.notes: The association’s standalone roundel survives in an archived copy of the official website. The September 2024 anniversary article shows the same mark over a photograph of the airpark.

artwork.label: Standalone full-colour roundel
artwork.locator: Homepage logo JPEG, captured by Internet Archive on January 22, 2024
artwork.verification: The archived 1831 × 1187 JPEG is held as published.

artwork.label: Roundel in Totem Times
artwork.locator: Page 3, roundel on the anniversary photograph
artwork.verification: The roundel is on the anniversary article’s composite photograph.

airports.name: Courtenay Airpark Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: The association describes the land runway and floatplane ramp together. The Courtenay Airpark roundel is the lead for shared branding.

airports.name: Creston Valley Regional Airport
airports.notes: Server returned PNG bytes despite the WebP URL. The 255 × 95 mark includes mountains, a sun, aircraft, CAJ3, and railway-track lettering. The Town's 2025 master plan uses the consultant's logo. The Airport Society is the lead for artwork in a larger or vector format.

airports.name: Dease Lake Airport
airports.notes: 250 × 150 transparent YDL signature with coloured arcs. Airport Improvement Project posters also carry the 250 × 150 raster. The Stikine Airport Society and TNDC are leads for the master artwork.

airports.name: Delta Heritage Airpark
airports.notes: 960 × 300 photo composite with an arched name and airplane emblem. The management committee and Recreational Aircraft Association Chapter 85 are leads for a detached master.

artwork.label: Delta Heritage Airpark website header
artwork.locator: Homepage header with alt Delta Heritage Airpark - CAK3

airports.name: Denny Island Aerodrome
airports.notes: The District hosts the Airport Commission's page. The Shearwater Resort and nearby water aerodromes have separate contexts.

airports.name: Duncan Airport
airports.notes: The operating club's official site identifies the airfield. Check club publications and entry signage for an airport signature.

airports.name: Elk Valley Regional Airport
airports.notes: The regional district website and budget report identify the facility under district branding. Check the master plan or existing airfield signage for a distinct mark.

airports.name: Fairmont Hot Springs Airport
airports.notes: 150 × 150 transparent airport signature with a maple leaf, aircraft and CYCZ script. The airport society's November 2025 letterhead is a vector lead. The agenda PDF was visible in indexed material and returned HTTP 403 to direct retrieval.

artwork.label: CYCZ script with maple leaf and aircraft
artwork.locator: Uncropped WordPress source for the homepage custom logo

airports.name: Fort Langley Airport
airports.notes: Official airport signature with an orange floatplane and navy lettering. The source SVG rendered as published and contains 55 paths and 17 polygons with no image elements.

artwork.label: Orange floatplane and navy Fort Langley Airport lettering
artwork.verification: Native SVG geometry, visually checked after rendering.

airports.name: Fort Langley Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: The airport owner presents floatplane docks and water access under its Fort Langley Airport identity. The provincial inventory lists land and water separately.

airports.name: Fort St. James Perison Airport
airports.notes: The District's airport page links its 2024 master plan. Terminal and dedication signage are further leads.

airports.name: Fraser Valley Regional Airpark (Hope)
airports.notes: The district's airport page carries the FVRD logo. Airpark building signage and district facility brochures are further leads.

airports.name: Ganges Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: Harbour Air markets this as a Salt Spring terminal. BC Air Access identifies a separate facility project in the Outer Harbour. Verify which dock and operator a specimen depicts.

airports.name: Golden Municipal Airport
airports.notes: Municipal information page and linked airport assessment provide leads for facility signage.

airports.name: Grand Forks Airport
airports.notes: Municipal airport operations manual confirms the designator. Current terminal photographs and City aviation materials remain open leads.

airports.name: Kaslo Aerodrome
airports.notes: Village identifies the registered aerodrome on its official page. Community signage and operators are the next sources.

airports.name: Kitimat Airpark
airports.notes: The volunteer operator uses a winged badge with the club's name. Standalone airpark identity remains unverified.

artwork.label: Kitimat Flying Club operator emblem
artwork.locator: June 1, 2026 council agenda, printed page 87, Attachment B, Kitimat Flying Club letterhead

airports.name: Likely Airstrip
airports.notes: District documents the community airstrip. Site signage remains an open lead.

airports.name: Mackenzie Airport
airports.notes: District's airport page and industrial subdivision material identify the airport. The marketing package carries the District's logo.

airports.name: McBride Airport (Charlie Leake Field)
airports.notes: The official site shows the Village masthead and an airport photograph. Look for separately branded dedication or airport signage.

airports.name: Merritt Municipal Airport (Saunder’s Field)
airports.notes: City airport page uses Merritt's municipal identity and an airfield photograph. The development plan and terminal signs are further sources.

airports.name: Nakusp Airport
airports.notes: The Village links the airport master plan it adopted in 2024. Check the plan artwork and signs.

airports.name: Nanaimo Harbour Heliport
airports.notes: Helijet locates this heliport at the Cruise Ship Welcome Centre. The designator comes from the OurAirports supplement. Resolve the nearby provincial Macmillan Bloedel point separately.

airports.name: Nanaimo Harbour Water Airport
airports.notes: Harbour Air's terminal listing gives carrier branding. The provincial layer also contains named operator-dock points. Keep the physical facility distinct from YCD and the separate Harbour heliport.

airports.name: Oliver Municipal Airport
airports.notes: Town manages airport and publishes operations manual and master plan. The South Okanagan Flying Club is a tenant and maintenance partner.

airports.name: Osoyoos Airport
airports.notes: The master plan uses the consultant's logo. The Airport Development Society's own publications are a lead for facility branding.

airports.name: Pemberton Regional Airport
airports.notes: The Village provides the airport information page and names Pemberton Hangar Holdings as the terminal operator. Terminal signs and Village airport documents are leads.

airports.name: Pitt Meadows Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: Airport society's Good Neighbour Program includes the land runways and water aerodrome under Fly YPK.

airports.name: Prince Rupert/Seal Cove Water Airport
airports.notes: The Prince Rupert Airport website describes the separate Seal Cove base and identifies Inland Air as a carrier. The Seal Cove Airport Society is a lead for facility artwork.

airports.name: Princeton Regional Airport
airports.notes: The Town's airport page identifies the Airport Committee. Committee documents and terminal signs are leads.

airports.name: Revelstoke Airport
airports.notes: Regional district manages the facility. The 2022 development plan cover displays the consultant's HM logo. Check terminal signage for a separate airport design.

airports.name: Sechelt Airport
airports.notes: The district airport page uses municipal branding. Keep land airport distinct from Sechelt's Porpoise Bay terminals.

airports.name: South Cariboo Regional Airport
airports.notes: Airport is at 108 Mile Ranch. District publishes airport information. Airport Commission and terminal signage are further leads.

airports.name: Squamish Municipal Airport (Don Patrick Field)
airports.notes: District airport page and strategic plan document municipal identity. The approved sign-replacement program is a lead for facility lettering.

airports.name: Texada/Gillies Bay Airport
airports.notes: Regional district facility page and airport plan use district identity. Treat Texada Aviation Museum and event marks as separate subjects.

airports.name: Tofino Harbour Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: Harbour Air documents its harbour terminal separately from the land airport YAZ.

airports.name: Vancouver Harbour Heliport
airports.notes: The operator's 2022 press release carries its own branding. Vancouver Harbour Flight Centre is the separate floatplane terminal.

airports.name: Vancouver Harbour Water Airport
airports.notes: Native white terminal signature. Downloaded SVG contains 32 paths and a rectangle, with no bitmap image elements. The signature identifies the passenger terminal at CXH. Look for the corresponding positive colourway before building the light preview.

artwork.label: White Vancouver Harbour Flight Centre terminal wordmark
artwork.locator: Homepage header, image alt Vancouver Harbour Flight Centre

airports.name: Vancouver International Water Airport
airports.notes: YVR presents the public Floatplane Facility as part of Airport South. YVR and the individual airlines have published branding.

airports.name: Vanderhoof Airport
airports.notes: District airport page provides official facility context. The airport's awards and flying club should be treated as separate branding evidence.

airports.name: Victoria Harbour (Camel Point) Heliport
airports.notes: Carrier-branded location evidence. Pacific Heliport Services has its own operator identity, shown in the letterhead for the separate Vancouver Harbour heliport.

airports.name: Victoria Harbour Water Airport
airports.notes: Federal airport and carrier terminal have separate roles. Current federal and Harbour Air pages show their respective organization branding. Check official water-airport or terminal sign artwork for a facility-specific signature.

airports.name: Whistler/Green Lake Water Aerodrome
airports.notes: Green Lake terminal is branded by Harbour Air. Look for earlier Whistler Air signage if documenting the operator history.
